title: The Elements of the World (stoicheia)
lead: The Greek phrase ta stoicheia tou kosmou in Galatians 4:3, 9 and Colossians 2:8, 20: the 'elements' of the world, which kept people in slavery before Christ. Readers take them as the four physical elements, the ABCs of religion, spirit powers over the stars, pairs of opposites (Martyn), or the basic rules of any religion-as-status.

sections.b: Stoicheia are things set in a row: letters, then basic parts of anything. (1) The four elements (earth, air, fire, water), which some worshipped (Wisdom of Solomon 13:2). (2) The ABCs, the first lessons (Hebrews 5:12). (3) Spirit powers of the stars and elements (Colossians 2:8; Testament of Solomon 8). (4) The pairs of opposites on which the old world was built (Martyn). (5) Any basic religious rules. The word is related to stoicheo, 'keep in line' (Galatians 5:25), and systoicheo, 'line up with' (Galatians 4:25).
